title: An import batch, from upload to committed or discarded
summary: Everything stages, nothing commits without review, everything rolls back by batch — and the raw upload is deleted at every exit, not only the successful one.
note: Two things this machine says that the stored `status` string does not. First, a commit with any failed row leaves the batch's persisted status as `staged` while stamping `committed_at` and marking the rows that succeeded — the batch is genuinely in a fifth condition, shown here as `partially committed`, and the code's own comment calls it partially staged so the owner can fix and re-commit (FR-020). Second, the raw upload is purged at every terminal exit, not only the clean one: committing, discarding and rolling back all call `purgeRawImport` (apps/api/src/services/imports.ts:541), because an address book, a calendar or a résumé is the most sensitive artifact in the system and re-importing is a re-upload, not a re-parse. Two boundaries worth stating: `rollbackImport` checks no status at all, so it will run against a discarded or already-rolled-back batch and simply remove nothing; and a batch that reaches `discarded` is never swept by retention, which only collects abandoned `staged` batches, so the row persists indefinitely with its raw content already gone. Direct GitHub synchronisation is deliberately not in this machine: it writes repository and skill nodes straight into the graph with `source_ref: 'github_sync'` and creates no batch document, so it never appears in batch history and cannot be rolled back through these endpoints — which makes the `'github'` member of the batch kind union (apps/api/src/services/imports.ts:89) a value nothing ever produces.

states.label: Nothing staged
states.note: The file is still on the person's machine. It is read client-side and posted as text, never as multipart, which is why the imports path mounts its own 15 MB body parser ahead of the global 2 MB one (apps/api/src/app.ts:51).

states.label: Staged
states.note: Parsed into rows, each scored against the existing graph for duplicates, and persisted as `imports` + `import_rows` + `import_raw_chunks`. Nothing is in the career graph yet. A row whose duplicate verdict is `probable` defaults to skip; everything else defaults to accept.

states.label: Partially committed
states.note: Some rows created records, at least one failed with a stated reason, and the failed ones stay `staged` so they remain retryable. The batch's persisted status is still the string `staged` — this is a distinct condition, not a distinct value — and `committed_at` is set even though the batch is not closed. The raw upload has NOT been purged, because only a clean run closes the batch.

states.label: Committed
states.note: A clean run: every accepted row produced a node, edge or atom, each tagged with the batch id as `source_ref`. The raw upload is purged, the duplicate scan cache is invalidated, and the search index is marked dirty.

states.label: Discarded
states.note: Nothing was created, and the raw upload is deleted with the decision. Discarding is treated as a deletion intent, not as an abandonment (FR-006). The batch document itself survives — retention only sweeps abandoned `staged` batches — so the history row remains with its content already gone.

states.label: Rolled back
states.note: Every node, edge and atom carrying the batch id as `source_ref` is soft-deleted — so they enter the ordinary 30-day trash, they are not erased — and the raw upload is purged. Re-importing means re-uploading the file.

states.label: Abandoned and swept
states.note: A batch left `staged` for longer than the 30-day retention window is hard-deleted by the purge, taking its rows and raw chunks with it through ON DELETE CASCADE. This is the only path that removes the batch document itself. It collects a partially committed batch too, because that batch's persisted status is also `staged` — the records its successful rows created are not touched, only the batch and its remaining staged rows.

transitions.label: POST /api/v1/imports
transitions.note: One of six kinds: linkedin, contacts, calendar, bookmarks, resume, aperture. The LinkedIn file is identified by its header shape rather than its name. Unparseable content is a 422 and stages nothing.

transitions.label: PATCH /api/v1/imports/:id/rows/:rowId — accept, skip, or edit the payload
transitions.note: The review step. A row already marked committed refuses to be edited.

transitions.label: POST /api/v1/imports/:id/commit — every accepted row succeeded
transitions.note: Refuses unless the batch's status is `staged`. Bundle edges are resolved last, once every accepted node has an identifier; a single rejected edge does not abort the rest.

transitions.label: Commit, with at least one row failing
transitions.note: One malformed row must never abort the batch. Failed rows keep their error text so the interface can explain the retry.

transitions.label: Fix the failing rows and commit again
transitions.note: Possible only because the persisted status is still `staged`, which is what the commit guard checks. Rows already committed are skipped on the second pass.

transitions.label: POST /api/v1/imports/:id/rollback
transitions.note: Sweeps live nodes, live edges and atoms by `source_ref`, soft-deleting each with the actor `import-rollback`, then purges the raw upload.

transitions.label: Roll back what the partial commit did create
transitions.note: The same endpoint. It checks no status, so it is reachable from here as well as from a clean commit.

transitions.label: Thirty days pass with the batch never committed or discarded
transitions.note: The retention purge collects `staged` batches created before the cutoff. It runs daily on an in-process interval, on demand through POST /api/v1/retention/purge, and from the command-line purge script.
